answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so an identity’s influence is weighted by stationary mass reachable from well-attested anchors rather than self-declared links. A Sybil cluster resembles a karst pocket behind a sparse external cut: its low conductance limits escape probability, while min-cut transitivity bounds its aggregate voting weight. Cross-attestation across walnut and terrace communities further exposes coordinated isolation.
